title: Ironbottom Sound as a wargame
label: A wargame played with the real forces. The record is on the other side of the table.

arena.note: West of Savo, some 1,100 m of water, 15 km from Savo and Cape Esperance: the midpoint of Washington and Kirishima at midnight, when Washington opened fire on the battleship in Atago's searchlights at 8,400 yards on 008° (ONI Part III); 2.5 km apart in the arena, on that bearing. The sky is the box's after moonset at 23:58, visibility about five miles (the box's weather).

japan.name: The Emergency Bombardment Force
japan.leader: Vice Admiral KONDŌ Nobutake 近藤信竹

formation.note: Kondō's four units as the box has them: the bombardment unit (Atago leading Takao and Kirishima) with its direct escort, the screening unit under Nagara ahead and the sweeping unit under Sendai; in the record they came round both sides of Savo, in the arena they come on together on 130°, Kirishima's course at midnight in the box. Tanaka's Oyashio and Kagerō, of the reinforcement unit, stay out.

phases.title: Kirishima opens fire
phases.text: Star shells burst over the American column and Kirishima's lookouts find a battleship: put two shells into her.

phases.title: Torpedoes from the screen
phases.text: Nagara's destroyers fire spreads at the American destroyers: put a torpedo into one.

phases.title: Searchlights
phases.text: Atago switches on her searchlights and holds a battleship in them: put three shells into her.

phases.title: Atago's torpedoes
phases.text: Atago and Takao fire spreads of Type 93 torpedoes: put one into a battleship.

phases.title: Finish her
phases.text: A battleship is burning and blind: sink her.

formation.note: Lee's single column, the four destroyers some 5,000 yards ahead of the battleships in the record and 1,200 m in the arena; on 295°, Washington's course before midnight in the box.

goal.text: Sink Kirishima and two cruisers before 10:00.

phases.title: Radar contact
phases.text: Washington has the leading ship on her radar: put a shell into a light cruiser.

phases.title: The destroyers' fight
phases.text: Walke, Benham, Preston and Gwin trade fire with the Japanese destroyers ahead: hit two of them.

phases.title: Searchlights
phases.text: Searchlights fix South Dakota: keep both battleships afloat.

phases.title: Washington unseen
phases.text: Washington is dark and unseen beyond the glare: put four 16-inch shells into Kirishima.

phases.title: Turn away from the torpedoes
phases.text: The last Japanese torpedoes are in the water: keep a battleship afloat to the end.

footnote: In the night of 14–15 November 1942 Walke and Preston were sunk, Benham was lost the next afternoon and South Dakota was badly damaged; Kirishima, wrecked by Washington's radar-directed 16-inch fire, capsized at about 03:20, and Ayanami was scuttled.
